dimensions.assessment: Affects all health insurance issuers, group health plans, Medicare Advantage organizations, and health insurance consumers nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: A health insurance issuer offering group or individual health insurance coverage... shall... submit to the Secretary... and publish on the public website

dimensions.assessment: Requires organizations to compile, publish, and submit detailed cost and revenue breakdowns and adhere to standardized plain-English formats.
dimensions.evidence: publish on the public website of such organization the following information in a consumer-friendly format specified by the Secretary

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative and compliance costs on health insurers and federal agencies to establish new reporting mechanisms and guidance, but does not specify direct federal spending amounts.
Amends the Public Health Service Act, the Social Security Act, and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to add disclosure and guidance mandates.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title XXVII of the Public Health Service Act and title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure health insurer accountability

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent ongoing reporting and disclosure requirements for plan years beginning on or after specified dates.
dimensions.evidence: with respect to each plan year beginning on or after January 1, 2027

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for health insurers to comply with new reporting rules.
Specific details on the exact content of guidance to be developed by the Secretary.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill impacts health insurance issuers, group health plans, and Medicare Advantage organizations by requiring new reporting, public disclosures of overhead and claim payments, and compliance with new plain-English standardized guidance issued by the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
